findings.claim: Lines 12 and 45 say header and footer are elements that create landmarks, without the condition that they do so only when scoped to the page body. Per W3C ARIA in HTML, a header or footer inside article, aside, main, nav or section maps to role=generic, not banner or contentinfo. The topic itself teaches article and aside (o1), so a learner can over-generalize to "every header is a landmark".

evidence.section: Document conformance requirements for use of ARIA attributes in HTML: header row
Document conformance requirements for use of ARIA attributes in HTML: footer row

findings.recommendation: Qualify the covers item, for example "Landmarks, and the page-level header, nav, main and footer elements that create them (a header or footer inside article, aside, main, nav or section is not a landmark)", or add that as a caution.
